facts.claim: User-based Conversion Lift compares conversions in a group that can see the measured ads with results in a group held back from those ads.
facts.intended_section: Describe what the test can answer

sources.support: Google describes treatment and control groups for downstream conversions.

uses.section_heading: Describe what the test can answer
uses.article_quote: a controlled comparison between a treatment group that can see the measured ads and a control group held back from them

facts.claim: Google does not offer Conversion Lift to every account and points advertisers to their account representative.

sources.source_title: Set up Conversion Lift based on users
sources.support: The setup page explicitly notes limited availability and the representative contact.

uses.article_quote: Conversion Lift is not available to every account and directs advertisers to their Google account representative

facts.claim: The current U.S. Google user-based setup documentation specifies at least 1,000 observed conversions, excluding supplementary data from that threshold.

sources.source_title: Set up Conversion Lift based on users
sources.support: The prerequisites distinguish observed conversions from supplementary conversions and state a floor of 1,000.

uses.article_quote: at least 1,000 observed conversions, excluding supplementary conversions from that threshold

facts.claim: Google's current U.S. user-based setup guidance lists a $5,000 USD minimum campaign budget for the study.

sources.source_title: Set up Conversion Lift based on users
sources.support: The public Account threshold section labels $5,000 USD the minimum campaign budget.

facts.claim: Google requires at least one compatible conversion action for the study.

sources.source_title: Set up Conversion Lift based on users
sources.support: The published account prerequisites include at least one compatible action.

uses.article_quote: include at least one compatible conversion action

facts.claim: Google Analytics web conversion imports are not supported for user-based Conversion Lift.

sources.source_title: Set up Conversion Lift based on users
sources.support: Google's unsupported setups table explicitly excludes GA web imports even when they contain user-provided data.

uses.article_quote: excludes Google Analytics web conversion imports for this user-based study, even when they contain user-provided data

facts.claim: Click-ID-only offline imports cannot support Google user-based Conversion Lift when a held-back person has no ad click to match.

sources.source_title: Set up Conversion Lift based on users
sources.support: The unsupported setups table explains why click-ID-only attribution misses people whose ads were withheld.

uses.article_quote: excludes offline imports relying only on click IDs: a person held back from the measured ads may have no ad click to match

facts.claim: Google's study power read uses account-level history, expected lift and planned settings including tracked actions, duration, budget and split.
facts.intended_section: Estimate the chance of a useful result

sources.source_title: Set up Conversion Lift based on users
sources.support: The study power inputs use the selected account history, not manager-level totals, plus the study's chosen settings.

uses.section_heading: Estimate the chance of a useful result
uses.article_quote: uses account-level history, estimated lift and selected settings including conversion actions, duration, budget and holdback split

facts.claim: When similar campaigns stay outside the study, people in the holdout may see those unmeasured ads, reducing the chances of detecting lift.

sources.source_title: Set up Conversion Lift based on users
sources.support: Google explains that holdback users can still encounter unmeasured campaigns when only a subset is included.

uses.article_quote: holdback users may still encounter unmeasured campaigns when only a subset is included, making lift harder to detect

facts.claim: Google notes that a larger holdout may increase the measurement sample while forgoing more ad opportunities, and a small holdout may take longer.
facts.intended_section: Estimate the chance of a useful result

sources.source_title: Set up Conversion Lift based on users
sources.support: The documented holdout tradeoff covers sample size, timing and opportunity cost.

uses.section_heading: Estimate the chance of a useful result
uses.article_quote: a larger holdback may increase the measurement sample while forgoing more ad opportunities, whereas a smaller holdback may require longer

facts.claim: Google recommends selecting a duration that captures the typical time from ad impression to the conversion being measured.
facts.intended_section: Estimate the chance of a useful result

sources.source_title: Set up Conversion Lift based on users
sources.support: The Study duration guidance ties design to average conversion lag.

uses.section_heading: Estimate the chance of a useful result
uses.article_quote: the period should capture typical conversion lag

facts.claim: Google recommends using upper-funnel actions as secondary measures when bottom-funnel events lack volume.
facts.intended_section: Choose the primary inquiry and secondary diagnostics

sources.source_title: Set up Conversion Lift based on users
sources.support: The conversion categories guidance explicitly labels upper-funnel metrics secondary when bottom-funnel data is sparse.

uses.article_quote: suggests upper-funnel actions as secondary measures when lower-funnel volume is sparse

facts.claim: Low conversion counts in the control group can make relative lift appear very large, and Google provides an interval around the result.

sources.source_title: Understand your Conversion Lift based on users measurement data
sources.support: Google warns about large relative lift with low-control activity and describes credible/confidence intervals.

uses.section_heading: Read a final result against the decision rule
uses.article_quote: low control conversion counts can produce unusually large relative-lift estimates and provides confidence intervals to help interpret results

facts.claim: Google recommends waiting until a user-based study ends before relying on its cumulative results.

sources.source_title: Understand your Conversion Lift based on users measurement data
sources.support: Google notes interim cumulative data can appear and recommends waiting to the end for the most accurate result.

uses.section_heading: Read a final result against the decision rule
uses.article_quote: recommends waiting until the study ends for the most accurate lift result, even though cumulative results may appear during it
